title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page records one standard construction, apparently a building block for the homotopy theory of cell maps (heading 'Homotopie sur les cartes cellulaires'). X is a space and G a group acting on it. Grothendieck defines the equivariant fundamental groupoid Π_1(X,G):
- Objects: the points x of X.
- Morphisms: Hom(x,y) is the set of pairs (ℓ,g), where g ∈ G and ℓ: gx → y is an arrow ('Fl' = flèches) of the ordinary fundamental groupoid Π_1X.
- Composition: given ℓ: gx → y and ℓ': g'y → z, set (ℓ',g')(ℓ,g) = (ℓ'∘g'(ℓ), g'g). Here g'(ℓ): g'gx → g'y is the transported path.

This is the semidirect-product groupoid Π_1X ⋊ G. Equivalently, it is the Grothendieck construction of the functor BG → Grpd sending the single object to Π_1X. It is also the fundamental groupoid of the quotient stack [X/G], i.e. the orbifold fundamental groupoid.

In context, X would be a (topological) map, or the surface carrying it, with G its automorphism group. The point is to treat 'maps up to symmetry' via the orbifold quotient. This links to the section list on the next page: groups Π_{0,3}, groups with signature (orbifold fundamental groups), and the fundamental 2-groupoid.

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of a G-space defined as pairs (path gx→y, g) with twisted composition
ideas.modern_name: Semidirect product / action groupoid Π_1X ⋊ G; fundamental groupoid of the quotient stack [X/G] (orbifold fundamental groupoid)
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Brown, P.J. Higgins (orbit groupoids, 1960s-70s); folklore; Grothendieck construction (SGA1)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in SGA1 (fibred categories, Grothendieck construction) and in the Esquisse d'un programme's use of orbifold/Teichmüller groupoids; the explicit formula is not known to me from a published text

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard textbook definition of the equivariant (orbifold) fundamental groupoid, written down as a lemma for the theory of maps (dessins). It contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The faint text in the upper half of the page is bleed-through of the next page's table of contents. It does not belong to this page.
